neighbours.label: the start of a quoted saying or scripture in religious or scholarly prose (opening quotation mark after 'he said:')
fire: The Prophet said to his companions: "Seek knowledge from the cradle to the grave."
In his letter the apostle wrote, "Love is patient, love is kind."
As the old commentator points out, "The host of young men is like the dew."
Then the teacher stood and declared, "He who is humble shall be raised."
Luther later recalled, "There I began to understand the righteousness of God."
The rabbi answered the student, "What is hateful to you, do not do to others."
Additionally, the scholar has stated, "Charity begins with the neighbour."
And the psalmist sings, "The Lord is my shepherd, I shall not want."
quiet: The Prophet taught his companions to seek knowledge throughout their lives.
In his letter the apostle wrote at length about patience and kindness.
As the old commentator points out, the young men are compared to dew.
Then the teacher stood and explained that humility leads to honour.
Luther later recalled how he came to understand the righteousness of God.
The rabbi told the student not to do to others what he himself hates.
Additionally, the scholar has written that charity begins with the neighbour.
And the psalmist describes the Lord as a shepherd who provides for all.
